config_verbatim:
# The prime-rel baseline, and the first arm here that is genuinely
# comparable to `vss-control`.
#
# ## Why this replaces the no-relations arms as the base
#
# Every locally-embedded arm before this one -- nomic, Nemotron and
# `qwen-wholedoc` -- embeds `get_doc_info(node_id, add_rel=False)`: name,
# type, source, details, and nothing about what the node is connected to.
# `vss-control`'s precomputed ada-002 vectors are over the `add_rel=True`
# text, which appends a `- relations:` block naming every neighbour grouped
# by relation type.
#
# PRIME's queries name related entities explicitly ("a gene that interacts
# with X and is associated with Y"). Those names appear in the answer's own
# document ONLY in the relations version. So the gap between `vss-control`
# (0.23057 dense mrr) and every local arm (0.182-0.216) was never a clean
# model comparison -- ada-002 was reading a richer corpus. The local arms
# were retrieving against text with the answer's distinguishing features
# removed.
#
# Two pieces of evidence from data already collected, before this arm ran:
# lexical beats dense on 5 of 9 arms, and the clearest exception is
# `vss-control` (0.23057 dense against 0.18483 lexical, the largest dense
# margin in the table). BM25 matches surface terms either way; it is DENSE
# retrieval that needs the neighbour names. That is the signature of missing
# relational text rather than a weak embedding model.
#
# ## The chunker is `whole-document`, and that is the point
#
# `vss-control` is 1.00 chunks/node because STaRK's precomputed vectors are
# one per document. Matching that is what makes this cell a model comparison
# instead of a model-and-granularity comparison.
#
# It is also what the corpus needs. **The `- relations:` block sits at the
# END of each document**, so any cap severs the neighbour names first. This
# corpus is mean 1,761 chars with 19.5% over 2,400 and 8.1% over 5,000 -- a
# 2,400-char cap would split a fifth of the corpus at exactly the wrong
# place, fragmenting the signal the relations text was added to provide.
#
# qwen3-embedding-0.6b is served with `n_ctx 32768`, which takes ~99.9% of
# this corpus whole. The single 133,778-character outlier is handled by the
# engine's re-split (`MAX_RESPLIT_ATTEMPTS`) rather than by a character
# guess -- the server rejects it, the engine halves and retries. That is why
# no cap is stated here, and it is the mechanism B-TOKEN-CAP-1 was closed
# with.
#
# This is also why nomic is the wrong model for this corpus despite being
# ~3x faster: its 2,048-token ceiling forces a ~2,400-char cap, which splits
# that 19.5%. It would spend its speed undermining the experiment.
#
# ## Reading it
#
# `qwen-rel-whole` minus `qwen-wholedoc` is the contribution of relational
# text at a fixed model and a nearly fixed chunker -- `qwen-wholedoc` is
# 1.169 chunks/node against this arm's ~1.00, which is a real but small
# difference and the only impurity in the comparison.
#
# `vss-control` minus `qwen-rel-whole` is, for the first time, the embedding
# model and nothing else: same corpus text, same 1.00 chunks/node.
#
# Reads `data/prime-rel/`, whose nodes.jsonl is the add_rel export; queries,
# candidates and edges are symlinks to `data/prime/`, so there is one copy
# of each and no chance of the two datasets disagreeing about them.
name: qwen-rel-whole
dataset: prime-rel
split: test-0.1
chunker: whole-document
embeddings: qwen3-embedding-0.6b
dimension: 1024
aggregation: max
agent: dense
k: 20

# Qwen3-Embedding is asymmetric in a shape no other model here has: the
# corpus side takes NO prefix -- the empty string is the correct value, not
# an omission -- and the query side takes a one-line instruction followed by
# `Query: `, which is the format the model was trained with. Stated rather
# than defaulted so it reaches `config_verbatim`; a prefix that is not
# recorded is a number that cannot be reproduced.
document_prefix: ""
query_prefix: "Instruct: Given a query, retrieve relevant documents that answer the query\nQuery: "
